description: We are young passionate students from Tajikistan building an educational website to explore space, learn facts, build your own spaceship, and see real-time space stats. Our team: Muzaffar, software engineer with his own browser and U.S. Embassy’s American Space Khujand fellow; Bekzod, SMM specialist and ASK fellow; Damirbek, fluent English speaker, Camp Rising Sun finalist and ASK alumnus; Saboatkhon, FLEX alumna and ASK administration head.
summary:
LUNAR SHIFT
Our game takes you to the Moon, where you become an explorer and build your own lunar base near the South Pole. Your mission is to develop the base and make it a safe place to live.
At the base, you grow food in a special ecosystem and produce oxygen, which is essential for survival. You also manage energy: using an interactive wrist computer, you distribute power between life support, solar storm protection, greenhouse lighting, and communication systems. If solar panels get damaged, you have to repair them, while constantly monitoring radiation levels and your resources.
But the most exciting part happens outside the base. Your character steps onto the Moon’s surface and collects space debris. Instead of leaving this waste unused, you recycle it and use the materials to build a rocket that will carry your journey further.
Along the way, players learn real science: how researchers study life in extreme environments, including extremophiles like Deinococcus radiodurans, which can withstand radiation.
This game is not only about survival. It’s about protecting the space environment, recycling materials, and discovering new possibilities for the future of space exploration. We want to make space exploration more accessible and engaging, especially for younger audiences, by turning complex scientific challenges into an exciting game experience.
details:
LUNAR SHIFT is an immersive 3D simulation where players become an astronaut managing a base at the Moon's south pole. Your mission is to collect space debris, repair and launch a rocket, and maintain base systems like a biolab and solar array.

HOW IT WORKS

The player controls an astronaut in a 3D world. Core mission: collect space debris → recycle materials → build a rocket. Players grow food in a special ecosystem, produce oxygen, and manage energy using an interactive wrist computer (distributing power between life support, solar storm protection, greenhouse lighting, and communication). If solar panels get damaged, they must be repaired. Players must constantly monitor radiation levels and resources.

NASA DATA INTEGRATION

The game integrates real NASA data and resources, including:

NASA DONKI: used for solar flare and space weather data.

NASA OSDR (GeneLab): used for astronaut health and extremophile research (e.g., Deinococcus radiodurans).

NASA MSL Curiosity RAD instrument: used for radiation data.

NASA Moon Fact Sheet (NSSDCA) and LRO/LCROSS missions: used for accurate lunar environmental data.

NASA Blue Marble: used for Earth textures.

NASA Artemis / SLS: used as reference for rocket models.

NASA APOD, MEDA, RadLab, and Mars Trek (via API/links).

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

Unity Engine — 3D game engine and physics (exported to WebGL for browser play).

C# — main scripting language for gameplay and interactions.

Unity Starter Assets: Third Person Controller.

3D Models & Characters: Meshy AI (AI-generated), Quaternius (CC0).

Animations & Rigs: Mixamo (rigging and animation).

NASA APIs and data portals accessed via UnityWebRequest.

SI USE DISCLOSURE

Some 3D character models were generated using Meshy AI (AI image-to-3D generation). All AI-generated assets were reviewed and adapted by the team.
